thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, U.S. Stocks Lower as Wall Street Mulls Economic Data, Earnings

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, U.S. Stocks Lower as Wall Street Mulls Economic Data, Earnings
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Tuesday"s regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -1.3%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.5%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.7%
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): +2%
PowerShares QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -0.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 0.1%.
U.S. stocks were lower at session's half, as investors digested a number of economic releases and earnings reports.
The PMI manufacturing index came in as expected at 56.5 in April vs a prior reading of 55.6. Meanwhile, the ISM manufacturing index came in at 57.3 in April vs expectations for 58.6 and previous month's reading of 59.3.
And, construction spending posted a surprise 1.7% decline for the month of March vs estimates for a 0.5% gain and previous month's 1% increase.
Apple (AAPL), Gilead (GILD), Mondelez International (MDLZ), Yum China (YUM) and Snap (SNAP) will be releasing their financial results after the close.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 0.1% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were lower.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 0.5% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.4%.
Amazon.com (AMZN) fell marginally after the online retailer said it is set to create 2,000 technology jobs in Boston, expanding its hub in the east coast city with a focus on its Alexa virtual assistant and machine learning. The Seattle-based company will also be expanding into 430,000 square feet in the Boston Seaport district, with doors opening in 2021. Along with its order-fulfillment centers, Amazon has created about 3,500 in Massachusetts, with investment of more than $400 million since 2011. The price tag on the new office wasn't given.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.8%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 1.5% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 1.6%.
Pacific Premier Bancorp (PPBI) slipped some 2% after the company posted Q1 net income of $0.60 compared with $0.34 a year earlier and missing the $0.62 average estimate of analysts in a Capital IQ poll. Revenue totaled $88.9 million in the quarter compared with $82.9 million a year earlier. That also fell short of the $89.7 million analyst consensus.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 1.2% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 1.2%.
Franklin Electric (FELE) rose more than 2% after the firm reported Q1 earnings per share of $0.45, up from $0.33 during the year-ago quarter, and ahead of the Capital IQ consensus forecast of $0.43. Net sales for the quarter were $295.6 million, up from $ 220.3 million for the same period last year, and surpassing the analyst forecast of $290.7 million. The company said that based on higher growth assumptions, it was raising its full-year 2018 estimate for earnings per share to a range of $2.27 to $2.37, from the $2.16 to $2.28 provided in previous guidance.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) fell 1.2% and other industrial funds Vanguard Industrials (VIS) and iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), were in the red.
Domtar (UFS) rose marginally after the company reported Q1 earnings of $0.86 per share, up from $0.32 during the same period last year. The result easily beat the Capital IQ consensus forecast of $0.73. Consolidated sales for the quarter were $1.35 billion, up from $1.3 billion during the year-ago quarter. That was ahead of the analyst forecast of $1.34 billion. The company said its paper shipments should benefit from the announced industry capacity closures for the remainder of the year, and it expects to benefit from recently announced pulp and paper price increases. It also said that Q2 will be affected by seasonally higher maintenance activity in its pulp and paper business as it moves into the annual shutdowns at some of its major facilities. Additionally, personal care is expected to be negatively impacted by higher raw material costs and an unfavorable tender balance.
Commodities
Crude was down 1.3%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.9%. Natural gas was up 1.7% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 1.5%.
Gold was down 1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.7%. Silver was down 1.7%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 1.3%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 1.2% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were firmer.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 1% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in negative territory.
HanesBrands (HBI) fell nearly 7% after the consumer goods company reported stronger-than-estimated Q1 earnings as revenue improved and also topped forecasts. Adjusted EPS decreased 10% to $0.26 in the March quarter, but beat the $0.24 average estimate of analysts surveyed by Capital IQ. Q1 sales increased 7% to $1.47 billion, surpassing the analyst consensus of $1.43 billion. Moving forward, the company expects Q2 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.44 to $0.46, and sales in the range of $1.7 billion to $1.725 billion. Analysts had projected $0.47 of EPS and $1.71 billion of sales. The company anticipates FY18 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.72 to $1.80, and continues to expect FY18 sales of $6.72 billion to $6.82 billion. Analysts had forecast EPS of $1.76 and sales of $6.74 billion.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.01% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 1.5%.
AbbVie (ABBV) gained more than 5% after the drug maker reported it has submitted a marketing authorization application to the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for risankizumab, an investigational interleukin-23 inhibitor, being evaluated for the treatment of patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. Risankizumab is not approved by regulatory authorities and its safety and efficacy have not been established.
